repository_card.frontier: The canonical graph distinguishes formal, literature, heuristic and speculative knowledge. This sweep adds context references and a searchable source/bridge dossier without promoting existing confidence or solved status.
repository_card.bridge_hypothesis: Priorities: zeta kernels versus truncated positivity; universal SDP/disentangler obstructions versus code-restricted recovery; tree gauge fixing versus physical reflection; explicit Hodge classes versus prescribed incidence; planar words versus rooted factorial budgets. Each bridge has its own preserved and lost structure in the repository cards.
repository_card.next_finite_task: Retrieve a small subgraph from the referenced canonical nodes, choose one finite task from the cross-repository map, and record its actual outcome before any confidence promotion. All finite tasks in this sweep remain proposals.
repository_card.falsifier: Abandon a bridge when its dictionary drops an indispensable quantifier, positivity notion, target support, characteristic assumption or operational resource. Graph proximity alone supplies no implication.
repository_card.proposal_status: speculative; not executed or formally verified

sources.title: A new proof that more than $2/3$ of the zeros of the Riemann zeta function are simple and on the critical line
sources.publication_status: preprint; peer-review status not established in this sweep
sources.review_depth: v2: Theorem 1.1 and Proposition 2.1; submission history
sources.source_claim: Lamzouri reports unconditional asymptotic proportions above 67.25% for simple critical-line zeros and above 83.62% for distinct zeros. Version 2 adds an 88.76% bound for zeros that are simple OR on the critical line, plus a bound on the average of those two proportions. The mechanism is a Hilbert-space kernel inequality.
sources.limits: The union bound is not an 88.76% critical-line bound. None of these proportions proves RH or full prime-resolvent positivity. Version 2 was posted on 8 September; the first submission was 2 September.
sources.reuse: Bibliographic metadata and original synthesis only; no permission to train on linked full text is inferred.

sources.title: Simple critical zeros and distinct zeros of the Riemann zeta-function in short intervals
sources.publication_status: preprint; peer-review status not established in this sweep
sources.source_claim: Wang adapts the kernel method to intervals of length T^theta. Theorem 1.1 gives theta-dependent lower bounds; Theorem 2.2 supplies a short-interval pair-correlation estimate.
sources.limits: The useful bound depends on theta and is asymptotic. It is not the global 67.25% bound for every short interval or a certified finite-height zero count.

sources.title: Semidefinite extension complexity of the separable set, with applications to approximate disentanglers
sources.publication_status: preprint; peer-review status not established in this sweep
sources.review_depth: v1: introduction, Theorem 1.1, Corollary 1.2, Section 3 and formalization links
sources.source_claim: Gharibian, Hecht and Rudolph give dimension- and accuracy-dependent lower bounds for semidefinite representations of separable-state optimization in the HNW model. The paper links a companion Lean development.
sources.limits: The common feasible region and objective-independent embedding are essential. This is not a lower bound for every SDP or for unrestricted SAT circuits. The paper credits a stronger concurrent disentangler result to Bostanci et al.; its SDP result has a distinct scope. External Lean proofs were not rebuilt here.

sources.title: A quantum oracle separation between QMA(2) and QMA
sources.publication_status: preprint; peer-review status not established in this sweep
sources.source_claim: Bostanci and collaborators report a quantum-oracle separation of QMA(2) from QMA and derive exponential input-size requirements for approximate disentanglers with total error below one.
sources.limits: Oracle separation is not an unrelativized class separation. Universal coverage of separable states is much stronger than recovery of one reference state or a restricted code. First posted 2 September.

sources.title: A note on the noncommutative Hodge conjecture for graded matrix factorizations
sources.publication_status: preprint; peer-review status not established in this sweep
sources.review_depth: v1: Theorem 1.1, Corollary 1.2, Lemma 3.1 and Proposition 4.1
sources.source_claim: Lin and Zhang report rational Hodge results for sums of independently very general squarefree binary forms, with m>=2 and d>=7. Explicit matrix factorizations supply classes; monodromy controls their exhaustion.
sources.limits: Theorem 1.1 and Corollary 1.2 concern this particular very-general family. They do not settle general rational Hodge, identify every special parameter, or construct the repository's prescribed clean-nodal detector.

sources.title: A unified family of counterexamples to Batyrev's non-negativity conjecture on stringy Hodge numbers
sources.publication_status: preprint; peer-review status not established in this sweep
sources.source_claim: Dais organizes counterexamples to stringy-Hodge non-negativity in a parameterized hypersurface family and relates negative entries to primitive middle cohomology.
sources.limits: Stringy Hodge numbers of singular spaces and the standard rational Hodge conjecture for smooth projective varieties are different statements. This is a useful degeneration stress test, not a counterexample to rational Hodge.

sources.title: Non-Abelian string melting and thermalization in an open lattice gauge theory
sources.publication_status: preprint; peer-review status not established in this sweep
sources.review_depth: v1: model, thermalization discussion and strong-dephasing reduction
sources.source_claim: A tensor-network study couples 1+1D SU(2) gauge theory with matter to a gauge-preserving Lindblad bath. It finds nonmonotonic relaxation and derives an exclusion-process description in a strong-dephasing limit.
sources.limits: This is an open-system finite/truncated lattice setting, not pure 4D Euclidean Yang-Mills. A Liouvillian relaxation rate is not automatically a Hamiltonian gap, and the strong-dephasing expansion has its own regime.

sources.publication_status: preprint; peer-review status not established in this sweep
